newsitem.title: BELARUS: CIS court dismisses Moldova claim for Kazakh grain.
newsitem.headline: CIS court dismisses Moldova claim for Kazakh grain.

text.p: The Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) economic court turned down a claim by Moldova on Thursday for 17,300 tonnes of grain it said Kazakhstan owed for help gathering its 1993 harvest, court officials said.
But Haydar Talibov, head of the court, told Reuters in an interview that the case was dismissed on a technicality and that the court's authority should be broadened.

Talibov said Kazakhstan had sent a letter to the court saying its side in the case, from the agriculture ministry, did not have the authority to represent the government -- meaning the court did not have the right to consider the case.

"We turned down the case for technical reasons in line with existing rules, but of course it is our case and we must widen the competence of the high economic court," he said. The case fell outside the court's competence which considered only "cases on fulfilling economic obligations at inter-state and inter-governmental levels," court advisor Mariya Pronina said.
The court, which reviews claims between the 12 former Soviet republics grouped in the CIS, has upheld similar cases against Kazakhstan brought by Belarus and Russia.

In October 1996 Kazakhstan was told to give Russia 39,000 tonnes of grain and 37 billion roubles for agricultural technology. In 1995 it ruled Belarus should receive 814,000 tonnes of grain for help gathering Kazakhstan's harvest in 1993.

Talibov said the court had no mechanism to enforce its rulings, though Kazakhstan had complied in the Belarussian and Russian grain cases, and a mechanism would be considered at a CIS summit which has been postponed from January 29.
